description: Four polyphonic inputs and four polyphonic outputs with 10 logic gate slots routed between them.

params.text: Picks the logic gate in that slot; drag up and down to change it, and right-click for its truth table and to delete or shuffle the slot.
Picks where that input of the gate is taken from: a fixed low, one of the four device inputs, a fixed high, or the output of a gate earlier in the chain. Drag up and down to change it.
Picks what the matching device output carries: a fixed low, one of the four device inputs, a fixed high, or the output of any gate. Drag up and down to change it.

inputs.text: One of the four polyphonic inputs offered to the gate routing; with nothing patched in it presents 0V on every channel.

outputs.text: Carries whatever its output selector is routed from, with as many channels as the widest input.

notes: a new module has every gate slot set to Not Connected and every device output routed to the -ve Rail pad, so it passes nothing until you choose a gate and route the pads.
feedback cannot be routed inside the module, since a gate can only be fed from a gate earlier in the chain; patch a cable from an output back to an input for that.
right-click a gate slot for its own menu: Inputs / Outputs lists where each of that gate's four inputs is routed from, and Truth Table draws the gate's truth table.
the gate slot's menu ends with Delete and Shuffle Up on an empty slot, or Shuffle Down on a filled one to make room for another gate; the routing is adjusted to match.
menu: Copy — copies the whole circuit, gates and routing both, for pasting into a DO module of any size.
Paste — writes the copied circuit into this module, dropping empty slots where this module is smaller; it appears only after a Copy, and reads Paste (device is too small) where it will not fit.
Digital Voltage Range — a submenu of 0-1V, 0-5V, 0-10V, -5V to 5V and -10V to 10V, setting the pair of voltages used for low and high; an input reads high above the midpoint of the pair.
Visuals — a submenu of Blue, Dark and Light for the colour scheme, plus Flat for a look without the 3D shading. The choice covers every SubmarineFree module and is kept outside the patch.
